title: The US Needs a Data Strategy for the AI Era, but Should Not Copy China
text:
The US Needs a Data Strategy for the AI Era, but Should Not Copy China

Nikkei Asia

Kevin Frayer/Getty Images

The following excerpt is from an op-ed published in Nikkei Asia on September 17, 2026, written by Ran Guo, Affiliated Researcher at the Asia Society Policy Institute's Center for China Analysis (CCA), and Lizzi C. Lee, Fellow on Chinese Economy at CCA.In August, the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission handed Washington an alarming report. "The People's Republic of Data" argues that China has spent a decade building the machinery to turn data into capital, from rules that let companies book data as a balance sheet asset to state-run exchanges where data is bought and sold. It also advises Congress to take China's effort seriously, and craft a comprehensive data strategy of its own. Lawmakers ought to "consider whether U.S. accounting standards should recognize data as an asset," the report says.The report is right to note that Beijing moved early, but there is one problem: China itself is already moving beyond the model it is urging Washington to study.After years of treating data like a strategic commodity to be owned and traded, Chinese policymakers have reached a conclusion that many economists suspected all along: Data cannot be assetized ex ante.Read the full op-ed here.
